domain.name: adi_flex
domain.one_line: Periodic-review inventory with advance demand information (ADI) and flexible (early) delivery; joint ordering + allocation under demand crossover. Wang & Toktay (2008), Mgmt Sci 54(4).

demand.domain: integer >= 0; one draw per due-offset tau in 0..T_dl each period, independent across periods and across tau
demand.source: Wang & Toktay (2008) sec 2: customers order in advance, and demand observed in a period carries a due date up to T_dl periods out. ONE demand process indexed by its due-offset - the customer base is a MIX over offsets (sec 4), not a set of separate demands. Enumerating it as one quantity per offset would state the rendering, not the theory.

demand_rate.domain: real, [0, inf); one rate per due-offset tau in 0..T_dl
demand_rate.source: the arrival rate at each due-offset. A rate of 0 means the customer base has no customers at that offset; a base whose whole rate sits on one offset is HOMOGENEOUS (sec 3), any other mix is heterogeneous (sec 4). The homogeneous/heterogeneous distinction is a point in this vector, not a different model.

order.source: the replenishment control: a quantity placed once per period. The theory bounds it only below, at 0 - supply is uncapacitated, so any upper bound is a rendering choice

allocate.domain: integer >= 0 per component, one component per due-date class still ahead (due-offsets 1..T_dl): a vector of dimension T_dl. Component k at most the outstanding demand of its class; the components jointly at most the stock remaining once the due-now class is settled
allocate.source: sec 4: 'in addition to the ordering decision, the inventory manager now faces an allocation decision' - use surplus stock to satisfy observed orders due later, or carry it over for future orders that may have earlier due dates. The choice is over the crossover-eligible classes only: demand due now or next period cannot be crossed over by any future arrival, so serving those is a forced move (sec 4.2), and it is taken after the period's demand is observed - fulfillment is the last event of the period. sigma of sec 4.2 parameterizes the paper's PL *heuristics* for this decision (Table 1 classifies its four models by exactly this row, their allocation policy); it is a policy's knob, not the model's control, and until F7 this IR declared it as the decision.

inventory.domain: integer; unbounded below - demand that is due and unmet is backlogged, never lost
inventory.source: net inventory at the review point, the level holding and backorder costs are charged on

pipe.domain: integer >= 0 per component, one component per outstanding arrival offset k in 0..L - 1: a vector of dimension L, EMPTY when L = 0. Bounded only below, at 0 - a component inherits the order's own unboundedness above
pipe.source: sec 2: 'the vector W_i = (w_i, w_{i+1}, ..., w_{i+L-1}) is the supply pipeline'. One of the three components of the paper's state (x_i, W_i, V_i). Its evolution admits no control (eq. 1): the whole pipeline moves one position forward and the new order z_i is inserted in the last position. The dimension IS the supply lead time, so at L = 0 the state is (x_i, V_i) and there is no pipeline to carry - which is every instance this campaign has run.

adv.domain: integer >= 0 per component, one component per due-offset j in 0..T_dl - 1: a vector of dimension T_dl. Bounded only below, at 0
adv.source: sec 2: 'vector V_i = (v_i^i, ..., v_i^{i+T-1}) is the advance demand profile, where v_i^j, j >= i, is the unsatisfied advance demand at the beginning of period i that is due by period j'. The third component of the paper's state, and the one that distinguishes this model from a classical inventory problem: demand that is unmet but not yet due sits here at no charge, and only what is overdue reaches net inventory.

L.source: supply lead time, deterministic; sec 2. The numerics sweep it over 0..4

T_dl.source: demand lead time: the largest due-offset an observed order may carry. The paper writes this T; this IR reserves T for the planning horizon

K.source: fixed cost charged whenever a replenishment order is placed; there is no per-unit ordering cost after the Veinott reduction

h.source: holding cost per unit of positive stock per period; stock withheld from early delivery is charged like any other unit

p.source: penalty per unit per period on demand that is due and unmet

N.source: planning horizon in periods, with no salvage value or terminal cost at the end

discount.source: the discount factor alpha of the cost recursion (eq. 5); the numerics all take it to be 1. Declared on the objective as `discount_factor` (its schema home, spec Objective), not as a scenario constant: it is a property of the objective, not a swept design axis

out_of_scope: capacity limits on the replenishment quantity: supply is uncapacitated, so any upper bound on an order is a rendering choice and never a physical one
per-unit ordering cost: removed without loss of generality by the Veinott reduction, leaving the fixed cost alone
lost sales: demand that is due and unmet is backlogged and eventually filled
supplier reliability, crossover in supply, and partial delivery: the supply lead time is deterministic and an order arrives in full
perishability, obsolescence, and any age-dependent value of stock
salvage value or terminal cost at the horizon end
pricing, demand shaping, and substitution across customer segments: the replenishment quantity and the allocation are the only controls
cancellation, or revision of a due date, once demand has been observed
multi-item and multi-echelon coupling: one item, one stocking point
any limit on how much may be delivered early in a period other than the class's own outstanding demand and the stock remaining after the forced fills
dynamics: each period runs three events in a fixed order: place a replenishment order, receive from the supply pipeline, then observe demand and fulfill
an order placed in period i arrives at the receiving event of period i + L; L is deterministic, so replenishments never cross
demand observed in period i carries a due-offset tau in 0..T_dl and becomes due in period i + tau
forall tau in 0..T_dl: demand observed at due-offset tau joins the unsatisfied profile at due date i + tau and leaves it only when filled

exactly one fill is forced: demand due in the current period can only be served from stock on hand at that moment, so it is settled against inventory and any shortfall is backlogged. No other fill is compelled - the model places no rule on demand that is not yet due

forall tau >= 1: how much of the class due at period i + tau to fill early from the free stock is the ALLOCATION DECISION - a free choice, bounded by that class's outstanding demand and jointly by the stock remaining once the due-now class is settled; the model imposes no rule on it. Sec 4.2's cascade - serve the due-next class first, then hold a protection level back from the rest - is a heuristic POLICY over this choice, not a dynamic of the system. Filling the due-next class early is weakly optimal (nothing arriving later can carry an earlier due date, and shipping now saves a period of holding), but a dominated action is still an action
demand that is due and unmet is backlogged and charged p per unit per period; demand that is unmet but not yet due carries forward at no charge
cost in a period = K * indicator(order > 0) + h * max(inventory, 0) + p * max(-inventory, 0)
minimize the expected sum of per-period cost over N periods, discounted by discount

notation.x_i: inventory - net inventory at the review point (Wang & Toktay 2008 sec 2)
notation.W_i: the vector of outstanding replenishment orders, by remaining time to arrival
notation.V_i: the unsatisfied advance-demand profile, indexed by due date
notation.d_i^{i+tau}: demand observed in period i and due tau periods later
notation.z_i: order - the replenishment quantity placed in period i
notation.T: T_dl - the demand lead time. The paper's T; this IR reserves the identifier T for the planning horizon
notation.y_i: the post-order modified inventory position, u + z in the reduced coordinates of sec 3.2
notation.(s(V), S(V)): the state-dependent order-up-to policy proved optimal for a homogeneous customer base (Prop 2), with S independent of the profile and s decreasing in it (Prop 3)
notation.alpha: discount - the discount factor of eq. 5
notation.sigma_i^{i+k}: the protection level guarding the class due at period i + k - the PARAMETER of the sec 4.2 PL heuristics, which are allocation policies of the form a = clip(surplus - sigma, 0, outstanding). Not a model quantity, and since F7 not this IR's decision either: the decision is `allocate`, the quantity itself, for which the paper carries no single symbol. The paper abbreviates sigma_i throughout the T = 2 exposition (eqs. 18-19, eq. 20), where the vector has one component. Two earlier misreadings of this symbol are on record: sigma taken as a scalar (fixed at F4), and sigma taken as the decision - the heuristic's knob mistaken for the model's control (fixed at F7)
notation.lambda^tau: demand_rate at due-offset tau; rendered as the scenario constant `lambda_seg`, one vector of length T_dl + 1 rather than one constant per offset

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current period i; the episode ends when period == N (per-branch horizon constant: horizon.T resolves to N per instance)

state_variables.name: inv
state_variables.desc: net inventory x_i at the start of the period (pre-order review point); negative = backlog of overdue (due-now) demand only - unmet not-yet-due demand lives in adv, not here

narrowed.to: integer in [-N * demand.max, N * order_max], per instance
narrowed.by: implementation: observation-box envelope, DERIVED in adi_flex_gym.obs_envelope() rather than declared here - a bounds entry may only be a literal or the bare name of a constant, so an expression over N / order_max / the demand generator's max() is not expressible at this site (upstream gap: the schema's own comment advertises `20 * demand.mean`, which the validator rejects). The upper limit is certain - at most N orders land and nothing else adds stock; the lower is N periods of demand left unserved, at the generator's own practical bound. Both move with the instance, which a single frozen pair could not

state_variables.name: pipe
state_variables.desc: supply pipeline W_i = (w_i, ..., w_{i+L-1}); pipe[k] arrives at the R event k periods hence. The dimension IS the supply lead time (sec 2, eq. 1), so the vector is EMPTY at L = 0 and the state is (x_i, V_i). Per eq. 1 the pipeline shifts first and the period's order is appended last, which is why no slot beyond L - 1 is needed: the pre-F6 rendering inserted before shifting, so it carried max(L) + 1 = 5 slots for every instance - the last structurally zero, and all five dead at L = 0

narrowed.to: each slot an integer in [0, the order cap]
narrowed.by: implementation: per-slot observation bound, inherited from the order cap - a slot can hold at most one order. Same derivation, resolved per instance.

state_variables.name: adv
state_variables.desc: advance demand profile V_i = (v_i^i, v_i^{i+1}): unsatisfied observed demand due this period (adv[0]) and next period (adv[1]); the width is the demand-lead-time window T_dl

narrowed.to: each slot an integer in [0, T_dl * demand.max], per instance
narrowed.by: implementation: observation-box envelope, DERIVED in adi_flex_gym.obs_envelope() (see inv). A due class accrues draws only while it is ahead, which is at most T_dl periods; the model bounds the profile only below, at 0

info_fields.name: d
info_fields.desc: realized demand vector D_i observed this period, one component per due-offset tau in 0..T_dl (width T_dl + 1): d[tau] ~ Poisson(lambda_seg[tau]), drawn as ONE `independent` sample. The declared field and the draw now have the same shape; before v0.9.10 made a stage-level wrapper usable, the interface was this vector while the rendering assembled it from T_dl + 1 enumerated scalar draws.

placement.rationale: realized demand is folded into inv/adv the same period; no later transition reads the raw draw (mirrors inv_single's 'demand' placement). Was three scalar fields d0/d1/d2 until the F7 round consolidated the interface

info_fields.name: received
info_fields.desc: units received from the supply pipeline this period (R event)

info_fields.name: fills
info_fields.desc: units delivered ahead of their due date this period, PER CLASS (one component per due-offset 1..T_dl, width n_alloc) - the realized allocation, where `allocate` is the requested one. The two differ whenever the shared free stock binds before a class's own outstanding demand does, and they differ SYSTEMATICALLY on the homogeneous branch, where alloc_enabled=false forces the maximal fill and the allocate decision is inert: a record there shows whatever was driven in beside a fill it did not cause (F20). early_fill is this vector's sum.

info_fields.name: early_fill
info_fields.desc: units delivered ahead of their due date this period, TOTALLED over the classes the allocation decides (due-offsets 1..T_dl) - the REALIZED allocation, i.e. the allocate vector clipped component-by-component against the shared free stock (or the forced maximal fill when alloc_enabled=false); the flexible-delivery control

info_fields.name: surplus
info_fields.desc: free stock once the due-now class is settled - the allocation's budget coordinate, and (with outstanding) what the seq_mask mode's mask is computed from

info_fields.name: outstanding
info_fields.desc: outstanding demand of the class the allocation is currently deciding for - the allocation's demand coordinate. One class at a time: the seq_mask encoding asks the n_alloc components in turn, so this stays a scalar at any T_dl (paired with surplus, the budget still unspent)

decisions.name: order

type.rationale: paper treats all quantities as integers; user confirmed integer decisions (Phase-A interview 2026-07-10)

bounds.rationale: DERIVED FROM THE DYNAMICS, NOT MEASURED, and since v0.9.11 stated as the derivation rather than restated as a number. ceil(N*lam + 4*sqrt(N*lam) + 1) with lam = sum(lambda_seg) bounds the horizon's TOTAL demand, which is the most an order could ever be useful for: an order can only serve demand that still arrives, and at most N periods of it do. The claim is therefore true of instances nobody has run. Four sigma rather than the observation sites' six because a discrete action space is explored and slack is paid for in sample efficiency (F14/F15). Human-confirmed as a DERIVATION, not as a number - the operator's call (2026-08-18) was that a cap comes from the model and its dynamics, never from what the solved runs happened to need. The rationale this replaced was the anti-pattern: '>=2x headroom over the largest optimal order (order-up-to S<=36 at lambda=6 plus deep backlog)', every quantity in it an observation of instances already solved, silent on the first instance that outgrows it.

decisions.desc: replenishment quantity z_i placed at the O event; arrives at period i+L; fixed cost K if positive, no variable cost (paper eq. c(z)=K*1{z>0})

narrowed.to: integer in [0, ceil(N*lam + 4*sqrt(N*lam) + 1)], resolved per instance
narrowed.by: implementation: action-space cap. The model bounds an order only below, at 0 (supply is uncapacitated), so the ceiling is a rendering choice - but its value is a derivation the IR now carries directly (auto-mdp-solver#53, v0.9.11: an expression over constants resolves per instance). 107 at N=12, 235 at N=30, tracked automatically; the 15 per-instance restatements this replaced are deleted.

decisions.name: allocate

type.rationale: integer allocation quantities; user confirmed integer decisions (Phase-A interview 2026-07-10, carried through the F7 redefinition 2026-08-17)

bounds.rationale: the constant sizes the declared action space only: the LIVE upper bound is state-dependent, min(remaining surplus, class outstanding demand), enforced by the action mask - so the cap never binds a feasible choice. 20 covers the far-class demand support at the largest designed rate (P(Poisson(6) > 20) < 1e-6)

decisions.desc: allocation quantities a_i (paper sec 4: 'in addition to the ordering decision, the inventory manager now faces an allocation decision'): a VECTOR of dimension T_dl, component k = units of the class due at period i + k + 1 shipped early this period. ONE fill is forced and it is not in this vector: demand due in the current period can be served from nothing but current stock, so it settles against inventory before the decision is taken. Every class still ahead is a choice. Sec 4.2's cascade - serve due-next first, then protect - is a heuristic POLICY over this decision; filling due-next early is weakly optimal but dominated actions are still actions (F10, the same line F7 drew for sigma). Taken AFTER the period's demand is observed (fulfillment is the last event, sec 2), a strictly richer information set than `order`'s: the rendering is therefore two-step (advance1/advance2). Feasibility is state-dependent - component k at most its class's outstanding demand, the components jointly at most the free stock - which the Feasibility enum cannot express (upstream candidate); it is enforced by the seq_mask mode's action mask, computed in the mdp layer. At T_dl = 2 the vector has two components. When alloc_enabled=false (homogeneous branch) the allocation is not a live decision: fill-as-early-as-possible is provably optimal (sec 3), so the simulator forces the maximal fill. UNTIL F7 this slot declared sigma, the protection LEVEL - the sec 4.2 heuristics' parameter - which baked the PL policy family into the action space: every expressible policy was a PL policy, and RQ2's discover stance was unreachable by construction.

narrowed.to: a vector of n_alloc (= 2 at T_dl = 2) integers, each in [0, alloc_max], live range masked to [0, min(remaining free stock, class outstanding demand)]
narrowed.by: implementation: alloc_max sizes the declared Discrete space; the state-dependent feasible set is enforced by the action mask (spec sec 7.1, validity computed in the mdp layer). Narrowed a second time per instance, to the forced maximal fill, by design:alloc_enabled=false on the homogeneous branch

distribution.note: ONE demand process yielding the paper's demand vector D_i in a SINGLE draw: `independent` of poisson, one component per due-offset tau in 0..T_dl, each at its own rate lambda_seg[tau]. Components are independent but NOT identically distributed, which is exactly what this family exists for (proposed from this campaign as auto-mdp-solver#49, shipped v0.9.9; usable at stage level from v0.9.10 after #52). Until then the rendering enumerated one draw statement per offset and keyed the stage on tau - a dynamics local - which restated the T_dl = 2 design point in the dynamics body and cost the path_independence law. A rate of 0 is a degenerate always-zero component (the one-hot homogeneous instances) and still consumes its draw, so trajectories stay comparable across instances.

updates: received = pipe[0] if L > 0 else order
pipe = pipe[1:] + [order] if L > 0 else pipe
adv = [adv[k] + d[k] for k in range(1, T_dl)] + [d[T_dl]]
want = [min(max(av[k], 0), adv[k]) if alloc_enabled else adv[k] for k in range(n_alloc)]
cum = [min(sum(want[0:k + 1]), surplus) for k in range(n_alloc)]
fills = [cum[k] - (cum[k - 1] if k > 0 else 0) for k in range(n_alloc)]
adv = [adv[k] - fills[k] for k in range(n_alloc)]

per_step_components.name: order_fixed
per_step_components.desc: fixed ordering cost, no variable cost (Veinott reduction per the paper)

per_step_components.name: holding
per_step_components.desc: end-of-period holding on positive net inventory (incl. protection stock)

per_step_components.name: backorder
per_step_components.desc: end-of-period penalty on overdue backlog only; unmet not-yet-due demand in adv is not penalized

constants.name: lambda_seg
constants.desc: arrival rate per due-offset, indexed by tau in 0..T_dl - ONE vector, not one constant per offset. The customer base is a mix over offsets: a base whose whole rate sits on one offset is homogeneous (paper sec 3), any other mix is heterogeneous (sec 4). Its length is T_dl + 1, so widening the demand-lead-time window widens this vector rather than adding a sibling constant.

constants.name: L
constants.desc: supply lead time in periods (paper sweeps 0..4)

constants.name: alloc_max
constants.desc: RENDERING CAP sizing the declared allocation space, never the live bound: the feasible set is state-dependent (min of remaining surplus and the class's outstanding demand) and enforced by the action mask, so this constant cannot bind a feasible choice. 20 covers the far-class demand support at the largest designed rate (P(Poisson(6) > 20) < 1e-6). Was protect_max, the cap on the sigma decision, until F7 - where it DID bind: with surplus above 20 the agent could not choose to withhold everything, a rendering cap acting as a constraint on a decision the model leaves free

constants.name: T_dl
constants.desc: demand lead time: the largest due-offset an observed order may carry, and hence the width of the unsatisfied advance-demand profile. The paper's T; the identifier T is reserved for the planning horizon here. Fixed at 2 across every instance - the homogeneous branch varies WHICH slot carries the rate, not the window

constants.name: n_alloc
constants.desc: number of allocation components = T_dl: one per due-date class still ahead (offsets 1..T_dl). Only the due-now class is forced - it can be served from nothing but current stock - so every other class is a decision. Derived from T_dl, so widening the demand-lead-time window widens the allocation decision with it. The count is unchanged from n_protect - sec 4.2's one-protection-level-per-eligible-class ('when T > 2, more than one protection level is needed') counts the same classes - but F7 redefined what each component IS: the quantity allocated, not the heuristic's reserve parameter. Was a literal 1 until F4.

constants.name: h
constants.desc: holding cost per unit per period (paper sweeps 1/3/5)

constants.name: p
constants.desc: backorder penalty per unit per period on overdue demand (paper sweeps 9/19/29)

constants.name: N
constants.desc: planning horizon in periods: 12 heterogeneous (paper sec 4.3), 30 homogeneous (Fig 3); horizon.T='N' resolves to it per instance

constants.name: alloc_enabled
constants.desc: scenario-mode flag for the customer_base branch: true = heterogeneous (the allocation is a live decision), false = homogeneous (fill-as-early-as-possible is provably optimal per paper sec 3, so the simulator forces the maximal early fill and the agent decides ordering only; the gym drops the allocation phase). Was sigma_enabled - the same split, stated as 'sigma forced to 0', which is the same policy: sigma = 0 IS the maximal fill

action_modes.name: seq_mask
action_modes.desc: Two-phase sequential encoding, one policy (MaskablePPO): each period the env takes an ORDER step at the pre-demand information set, then one ALLOCATION step per component at the post-demand set - all in a single shared Discrete(order_max + 1) whose per-step mask selects the live range: the full order range at the order phase, [0, min(remaining surplus, class outstanding demand)] at an allocation phase. The current phase is an observation feature, so one network conditions on which decision it is taking. The simulator is two-step per spec sec 1.1 - advance1 (order; ends with the demand realized) / advance2 (the full allocation vector; fulfillment and costs) - and the gym accumulates components against the residual before calling advance2: components share one information set, so the micro-steps between them are an action-encoding device (the slot pattern: several agent steps inside one information set, the phase carried as an observation feature), NOT extra MDP periods. At T_dl = 2 that is two allocation steps (one period = 3 agent steps), at T_dl = 3 three (4 steps) - n_alloc equals T_dl since F10, because only the due-now class is forced and every class ahead is a decision; alloc_enabled=false drops the allocation phase entirely (single-phase ordering env). Replaces the F1 modes `discrete`/`box`, which encoded (order, sigma) as one simultaneous pre-demand action - an information-set error: the allocation was committed before the demand it allocates against was observed, while the mdp consumed it after the draw.

action_modes.name: order_protection
bounds: max([0] + [ceil(sum((t-j)*lambda_seg[j] for j in range(t)) + 4*sqrt(sum((t-j)*(t-j)*lambda_seg[j] for j in range(t)))) for t in range(1, T_dl)])
action_modes.desc: ONE-SHOT PROTECTION-LEVEL encoding of the SAME two decisions, and the paper's own policy structure. The action is (order, sigma_1..sigma_{T_dl-1}), taken ENTIRELY at the pre-demand information set - one agent step per period against seq_mask's 1 + n_alloc - and the allocation that follows is mechanical. Decode: after advance1 realizes demand, available stock is poured into the priority cascade sigma_0, adv[0], sigma_1, adv[1], ..., sigma_{T-1}, adv[T-1]; a sigma box RETAINS stock (it stays in inventory), an adv box SHIPS it early. Formally, with rem initialized to the free stock once the due-now class has settled: for k in 0..T-1, rem -= min(rem, sigma_k); a[k] = min(rem, adv[k]); rem -= a[k]. SIGMA_0 IS IDENTICALLY 0 and is not part of the action: reserving ahead of the nearest class ahead holds stock while adv[0] goes unserved, with no more-urgent competitor for it and early shipment costless, so the unit is shipped next period anyway having paid holding for nothing - weakly dominated, the same argument F10 makes for filling due-next early. Hence n_sigma = T_dl - 1, which is the paper's own count: sec 4.2 after eq. 20 needs sigma^{i+1} AND sigma^{i+2} at T = 3. AT T_dl = 2 THIS REDUCES EXACTLY TO PL(sigma): the cascade gives a[1] = clip(surplus - a[0] - sigma_1, 0, adv[1]), which is sec 4.2's rule with the heuristic's sigma, so PL(sigma) is the CONSTANT action sigma_1 = sigma where seq_mask needs a state-dependent function of two observed features. That is the whole point of the mode and the reason it is a design axis rather than a convenience. THIS IS F1'S SHAPE, DELIBERATELY, AND IS NOT F1'S DEFECT. The withdrawn `discrete`/`box` modes also committed (order, sigma) pre-demand, but as an UNDECLARED information-set error: the gym committed before the draw while the mdp consumed after it, and nobody intended the restriction. Here the restriction is the declaration. It is real and bounded: sigma cannot condition on the realized demand, so the policy class is strictly SMALLER than seq_mask's (the allocation still depends on the draw, through surplus and adv in the clip - only sigma itself cannot). It is strictly LARGER than the PL family, since sigma may vary with the pre-demand state where the paper's heuristics hold it constant. PL(constant sigma) < order_protection < seq_mask, and whether the middle term costs anything is the question the mode exists to ask. TWO FURTHER RESTRICTIONS, both declared rather than discovered: the cascade fixes a nearer-first PRIORITY ORDER, so unlike seq_mask this mode cannot express 'skip adv[0], serve adv[1]' (dominated by the same argument as sigma_0, but seq_mask does not need the argument); and the sigma cap is a 4-sigma tail, so the mode is onto the feasible set only up to that tail. SIGMA BOUND, DERIVED FROM THE DYNAMICS and stated as the derivation rather than a number (auto-mdp-solver#53): sigma_t is held instead of serving adv[t], so it can only ever be useful for demand arriving LATER but due SOONER than adv[t]. Demand arriving s periods out at due-offset j is due before adv[t] iff j <= t - s, so over s = 1..t the protected quantity is sum_{j<t} (t-j)*D[j] - a WEIGHTED sum of independent Poissons, mean sum (t-j)*lambda_j and variance sum (t-j)^2*lambda_j, NOT itself Poisson, which is why F14's aggregate-a-tail rule is applied with weights rather than by scaling a per-period bound. At FOUR sigma: the action-space multiple, not the observation sites' six, because a discrete action space is explored and slack is paid in sample efficiency. Reserving beyond it holds stock no arriving demand could preempt adv[t] for, so it pays holding while adv[t] goes unserved - dominated up to the tail, the same standard order_max is held to. VALIDATED INDEPENDENTLY against the paper's own plmax = min{s : P(d0 > s) < 0.001}: the derivation gives 16/14/12/8 on het_exp0/1/2/4 against plmax 15/13/11/8 - two routes to the same tail agreeing within 1, exactly on het_exp4. Degenerates correctly: 0 at T_dl <= 1 (no crossover-eligible class exists, so the [0] + guard is load-bearing, not defensive) and 0 wherever lambda_0 = 0 (nothing can ever preempt), which is het_exp6/het_exp7 - and there all three heuristics independently give sigma = 0 too. NOT protect_max, which F7 removed: that capped sigma AS A DECISION at an unargued 20 and DID bind, forbidding withholding whenever surplus exceeded it. This caps an action ENCODING of the allocate decision, at a value argued from the dynamics. feasibility_strategy IS `none`, and that is the mode's other claim: pre-demand the components do not share a budget - surplus does not exist yet - so the feasible set is a fixed box and EVERY action in it is legal by construction. seq_mask needs a state-dependent sequential mask over a shared budget (measured: 3.01 of 108 actions legal at an allocation step, 21% of them forced). The constraint is not enforced here, it is dissolved: 'reserve sigma' already means 'as much as possible, no more'. A deployed policy therefore needs no mask and no import of mdp.valid_allocation, unlike seq_mask's. KNOWN GAP, second occurrence: the sigma -> allocate decode CANNOT BE DECLARED. Schema v1 refuses a per-component `transform` on a multi-decision mode, so this ships transform="" and the decode lives in prose and in adi_flex_gym. F30 recorded the same limitation for the withdrawn target mode; unlike F30's, this mode ships, so the gap is now load-bearing - no gate can verify the decode, which is why the acceptance test is bit-exact reproduction of PL(sigma) 341.26 on het_exp4 and of forced maximal fill against the exact DP 258.852305 on het_exp7 (lambda_0 = 0, sigma vanishes, and sec 3 proves maximal fill optimal there). DEGENERATES TO 0, AND SAYS SO. The derivation is exact and gives 0 wherever no reserve can exist - T_dl <= 1, lambda_0 = 0, and every homogeneous instance, where the allocation is not a live decision at all - which is 16 of the 30 declared instances, 4 of them with a live protection decision (het_exp6, het_exp7, het3_exp5, het3_exp6). It formerly carried a max(1, .) floor: schema v1 refused a bound with lo >= hi, so a discrete action with exactly ONE legal value could not be declared as [0, 0], and the gym mirrored the same floor so the two would not diverge. That floor was a concession to the validator and not part of the argument - the padded action reserved a unit nothing could preempt, dominated by construction. Upstream #69 (this campaign's proposal, shipped v0.9.30) made the predicate type-aware, so lo == hi is now a legal discrete bound and the derivation is declared as itself. On the four live-decision instances the protection space is Discrete(1): the mode reduces to forced maximal fill, which sec 3 proves optimal there, and that is now a property of the DECLARATION rather than something a test has to pin by hand.

action_modes.name: target_ip
action_modes.desc: ORDER-UP-TO encoding of the order decision, on the INVENTORY POSITION; the allocation is unchanged from seq_mask (quantity, post-demand, masked), so this mode isolates the ORDER encoding exactly as order_protection isolates the allocation encoding. Decode: the agent emits a target y and the env orders clip(y - IP, 0, order_max), where IP = inv + sum(pipe) is the inventory position - NOT on-hand, which coincides with it only at L = 0 (every het board) and would re-order stock already in transit at L > 0, so the mode stays correct on the parked L-sweep instances. Emitting y <= the reference means 'do not order', so the no-order action is expressible and the mode is onto the full order range. THE REFERENCE IS THE ARM'S OWN SUFFICIENT STATISTIC, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE MODE ADMISSIBLE. F30 built and withdrew a target mode whose decode computed u for EVERY arm, including `vec` - handing the raw arm the very transform RQ4 asks whether a network can rebuild, which would have made vec and vec_mip artificially equivalent and answered the tier-2 question by fiat. Splitting the mode in two removes that: this one hands `vec` only inv and pipe, which it already observes. The pairing is therefore a CROSS-AXIS CONSTRAINT, not a free cross-product: target_ip is coherent with `vec` and incoherent with `vec_mip`, which cannot see inv at all. Only the diagonal cells may be run, and RQ4 read across this mode compares (observation, action) PAIRS rather than observations alone - a coarser comparison, declared here rather than discovered. WHAT IT BUYS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: in a stationary problem the optimal target is near-constant, so an up-to encoding turns a stationary policy into a stationary ACTION, where the quantity encoding makes the same policy a sliding value q = y - reference that the network must track for no informational gain. But K = 100 here, so the optimum is (s,S) and NOT base-stock: a target fixes the MAGNITUDE (emit S) while the TRIGGER stays state-dependent, so this mode buys half the simplification, not all of it - strictly less than order_protection buys on the allocation, where the clip absorbs everything. F30's own measurement (the best CONSTANT target costs 2893 against the DP's 685, because a constant target orders every period and pays N*K in setup alone) tested one degenerate member of the class rather than the class, and does not settle it either way. ACCEPTANCE TEST, and it is unusually strong: the DP and AP benchmark policies are ALREADY order-up-to policies - adi_flex_benchmark_rule computes order = clip(y - u, 0, order_max) from a solver table whose columns are (i, vhat, s, S) - so the optimal policy is natively expressible in this mode's sibling target_mip and replaying that table through the decode must reproduce the solver's number to the float. KNOWN GAP: the target -> order decode cannot be declared (schema v1 refuses a per-component transform on a multi-decision mode), so this ships transform="" with the decode in prose and in adi_flex_gym - F30's limitation, on its second occurrence.

action_modes.name: target_ip_protection
bounds: max([0] + [ceil(sum((t-j)*lambda_seg[j] for j in range(t)) + 4*sqrt(sum((t-j)*(t-j)*lambda_seg[j] for j in range(t)))) for t in range(1, T_dl)])
action_modes.desc: BOTH encodings at once: order-up-to on the INVENTORY POSITION AND protection levels for the allocation, the full 'every decision is a level' form of this problem. It is the composition of `target_ip`'s order decode and `order_protection`'s cascade, with NO new decode of its own — which is why it was declarable at zero marginal risk once those two were verified, and why its acceptance test is the same replay run through both maps at once. ONE-SHOT, like `order_protection` and unlike the bare target modes: both decisions are taken at the pre-demand information set, so a period is ONE agent step (T~ = N, against the two-phase modes' N*(1+n_alloc)) and the within-period block is not rendered — there is no interior to describe. On this branch that makes the observation the narrowest the domain admits. Every restriction the two parents carry applies here and none is new: sigma committed pre-demand (so the policy class is strictly smaller than seq_mask's), sigma_0 identically 0, the cascade's fixed nearer-first priority, the 4-sigma reserve cap, and the order target's no-order SENTINEL at index 0 — needed because `y <= reference` stops meaning 'do not order' once the reference goes negative, and with K=100 against p=9 the optimal policy genuinely declines to order under backlog. The reference is the arm's OWN sufficient statistic, so the observation pairing is a cross-axis constraint and not a free cross-product: this mode is coherent with `vec` and incoherent with the mip modes, which cannot see `inv` at all. feasibility_strategy is `none`: pre-demand the components share no budget, so the feasible set is a fixed box and every action in it is legal by construction — the constraint is dissolved rather than enforced, and a deployed policy needs no mask and no import of mdp.valid_allocation. KNOWN GAP, as for its parents: schema v1 refuses a per-component `transform` on a multi-decision mode, so this ships transform="" and both decodes live in adi_flex_gym, unreachable by any gate — pinned instead by bit-exact reproduction in adi_flex_action_mode_probe.py.

requires_memory.rationale: fully observed: (inv, pipe, adv, period) is the paper's own sufficient state (x_i, W_i, V_i); no latent source (human confirmed 2026-07-10)

obs_normalization.rationale: stationary features of heterogeneous magnitude (inv in [-400,400], pipe elements in [0,100], adv in [0,400], time_to_go in [0,30]); spec sec 8.3 says normalize

benchmarks.name: dp
benchmarks.basis: Backward induction over the (u, vhat) reduction of paper sec 3.2, u = inv - sum(adv) and vhat = total demand due next period, with Poisson tails truncated at mass < 1e-12 and renormalized. EXACT on the homogeneous branch (homog_*), where a single demand lead time makes the allocation relaxation tight and the recursion is the paper's own. Do NOT read it as exact on het_* - there the same table is the AP relaxation, declared separately as the `ap` arm REQUIRES dim(V-hat) = T - L - 1 <= 1 (eq. 11), which is what actually binds — NOT L = 0, as this basis and the script both claimed until 2026-08-27 (#E15). (T=3, L=1) is the same reduced shape as (T=2, L=0) and is solved by the same recursion: with a supply lead time the order lands at i+L, so eq. (14) charges the loss on the inventory at i+L+1 and its two demand aggregates span i..i+L rather than the period — everything ARRIVING in the window at rate (L+1)*sum(lambda), and the part of it DUE by i+L at rate sum_k (L+1-k)*lambda_k — discounted by alpha^L per eq. (12). Both are plain sums of independent Poissons and both collapse at L = 0 to exactly what the L=0 path always computed, which is asserted against the recorded values rather than assumed. A reduced state two or more v-hat components wide still needs a wider DP and is still refused.

benchmarks.name: ap
benchmarks.basis: The allocation-postponement relaxation of paper sec 4.1: early delivery is costed as if the allocation decision could be deferred, which drops a constraint the deployed policy must respect. A LOWER bound on optimal cost for a heterogeneous customer base (het_*), unattainable by construction. Same backward induction as `dp`, read under the relaxed interpretation REQUIRES dim(V-hat) = T - L - 1 <= 1 (eq. 11), which is what actually binds — NOT L = 0, as this basis and the script both claimed until 2026-08-27 (#E15). (T=3, L=1) is the same reduced shape as (T=2, L=0) and is solved by the same recursion: with a supply lead time the order lands at i+L, so eq. (14) charges the loss on the inventory at i+L+1 and its two demand aggregates span i..i+L rather than the period — everything ARRIVING in the window at rate (L+1)*sum(lambda), and the part of it DUE by i+L at rate sum_k (L+1-k)*lambda_k — discounted by alpha^L per eq. (12). Both are plain sums of independent Poissons and both collapse at L = 0 to exactly what the L=0 path always computed, which is asserted against the recorded values rather than assumed. A reduced state two or more v-hat components wide still needs a wider DP and is still refused.

benchmarks.name: rule
benchmarks.basis: Real policies under the real information set: `myopic` as the floor arm, plus the paper's protection-level heuristics PL(0)/PL(sigma)/PL(Sigma) of sec 4.2, whose ordering follows the AP-relaxation y* table and whose protection level is a fixed rule A uniform-random policy is NOT among these: it draws over the action space, so its value tracks order_max rather than the problem, and it moved twice in one day for reasons that had nothing to do with policy quality. It remains runnable as a diagnostic (--policy random) and is reported nowhere.

tier2.claim: on the heterogeneous branch the learned allocation is PL-shaped: allocated quantity ~= clip(surplus - sigma, 0, class outstanding) for a recoverable protection level sigma, rather than an arbitrary function of state. Only askable since F7: with sigma as the action every expressible policy was PL-shaped by construction, so agreement demonstrated nothing
tier2.instrument: adi_flex_policy_probe.py: sweep the crowned artifact's allocation over (surplus, outstanding) at fixed periods, fit sigma, report the structural-form statistic and the fitted level against the PL(0)/PL(sigma)/PL(Sigma) references across the het_exp mixes

tier2.structure: allocation rule beyond a constant protection level
tier2.claim: the learned allocation varies where a fixed-sigma PL policy cannot (with state and time-to-go), and the rule extracted from it, paired with the AP ordering policy and scored as a feasible benchmark arm, beats PL(sigma) on the shared seed protocol. Scope (human-decided 2026-08-17, headroom probe declined): PL(sigma) sits ~1.3% above the AP lower bound and an unknown share of that bracket is relaxation slack, so the certifiable claim is 'beats PL(sigma) on the shared protocol', never 'near-optimal'
tier2.instrument: the rule extracted from the probe's allocation surface, added to adi_flex_benchmark_rule.py as a policy and scored at the full protocol (mab #E26 precedent: the fitted rule is a first-class sec 9 benchmark arm)

tier2.claim: on the homogeneous branch, where Wang & Toktay Prop 2 proves an (s(V), S(V)) policy optimal, the learned policy recovers that structure - S independent of the advance-demand profile and s decreasing in it (Prop 3)
tier2.instrument: policy readback on the crowned artifact, overlaid on the exact DP's own s/S table at the same instance

tier2.structure: the modified inventory position as a sufficient statistic
tier2.claim: Wang & Toktay's central structural result is that the state (x_i, W_i, V_i) collapses onto the MIP u_i = x_i + sum(W_i) - sum(V_i) (eq. 7), complete on its own when T <= L + 1 (Prop. 1) and needing only V~ = adv[L+1:] beside it when T > L + 1 (eq. 11). The claim under test is that a policy trained on `vec` - the raw state, from which the MIP is NOT recoverable, since only inv + sum(pipe) survives the transform - matches one trained on `vec_mip`, which is handed the statistic. This is a strictly LOSSY compression, unlike clark_scarf's raw/echelon change of coordinates: if the two arms tie, the network rebuilt a transform the paper had to prove
tier2.instrument: paired PPO arms at obs_mode in {vec, vec_mip}, same seeds and protocol, on both branches; the design axis is the paper's own case boundary - 12 registry instances are Case 1 by the declared width (T_dl <= L + 1 - exactly the homog_L1..L4 grid), where mip_tail_slots is 0 and `vec_mip` is the scalar u_i plus the within-period block, and 17 are Case 2, where V~ is one component wide. By the EFFECTIVE lead time (the largest offset carrying a positive rate) the split is 16/13 instead; the rendering must use the declared width, so on the 4 one-hot L=0 instances that differ it carries an identically-zero tail the theory does not need - conservative, never insufficient. A tie on Case 1 is the strong reading (the whole profile was discarded and nothing was lost); a gap on Case 2 with a tie on Case 1 would locate the loss exactly where eq. (11) predicts it

assumptions_log: UNIFIED MODEL: the homogeneous (sec 3) branch is encoded as one-hot demand-rate instances of the heterogeneous T_dl=2 model - lambda one-hot*6 at slot T (paper's demand lead time), alloc_enabled=false forcing the maximal early fill (FCFS fill-as-early-as-possible, provably optimal for homogeneous customers; pre-F7 this was stated as 'sigma forced to 0', the same policy). Cross-check: het_exp7 (0,0,6) under a maximal-fill allocation policy must be trajectory-identical to homog_L0_T2 modulo N.

FIVE-CASE DYNAMICS AS MIN/MAX CASCADE: paper eq. (18)-(19)'s five cases are implemented branch-free - the two forced fills (due-now, then due-next: exactly two at any T_dl, since nothing arriving later can cross them), then the allocation over the crossover-eligible classes, each component clipped to its own outstanding demand and jointly to the surplus they share. Verified algebraically equivalent case-by-case, and equal to eqs. (2)-(4) under the maximal fill. The shared-budget clip is rendered as a prefix sum (cum/fills) rather than a running residual: identical values, but expressible without a fold. Until F7 the cascade wrote the protection rule (fill above sigma_eff) as the dynamic itself; until F10 it was written for a single eligible class.

HORIZON: horizon.T names the scenario constant N (30 homog / 12 het, per paper), resolved per instance via MdpBlock.horizon_T() - schema extension 2026-07-10; previously encoded as a fixed T=30 cap plus gym early-termination at period >= N.
MODE STANCE (human-decided): homogeneous and heterogeneous are independent branches reported on separate leaderboards; a cross-branch head-to-head is meaningless.

DECISIONS (human-confirmed): integer z in {0..100} and sigma in {0..20}; caps chosen to never bind at the optimum (order-up-to S<=36 at lambda=6; P(Poisson(6)>15)<0.001 bounds useful protection). sigma applies only to the farthest (due-offset-2) class per sec 4.2 with T_dl=2.
BACKORDER SEMANTICS: only overdue (due-now) unmet demand is backlogged into negative inv and penalized at p per period; unmet not-yet-due demand carries in adv unpenalized (paper eq. 18 case 1).

COSTS at END_OF_PERIOD on end-of-period inv: K*1{z>0} + h*inv+ + p*inv-; no variable order cost (Veinott reduction). discount alpha=1 per all paper numerics (constant recorded for future sweeps; enters DP recursion / RL gamma, not per-step exprs).
INITIAL STATE (human-confirmed): empty system (0, zeros, zeros) per Figure 4's stated initial state.
PAPER'S T (demand lead time) is implicit: position of the nonzero lambda slot (homogeneous) or fixed window 2 (heterogeneous); the identifier 'T' is reserved for the horizon in the IR namespace.

SCENARIO SET (human-confirmed): 15 homog (L,T)-grid instances (Fig 4) + het_exp1..6 demand mixes (Table 2, base costs) + validation endpoints het_exp0/het_exp7; the paper's 540-cell sweep (exps 2-5 x L0-4 x K{50,100,200} x h{1,3,5} x p{9,19,29}) stays axis-registered, cells addable as one-line instances.

SAMPLERS (human-confirmed strategy: both specialist and generalist): homog_grid = uniform over the 15 homog instances; het_mix = uniform over het_exp1..6; implemented in Phase B as AdiFlexScenarioSampler (scenario stream_id 0) - the IR schema has no sampler slot.

TRAIN/EVAL (human-decided): both strategies per branch - specialist trained on the base instance (homog_L0_T2 / het_exp4) and a generalist trained on the branch sampler, each evaluated per instance against DP (homog: exact state-dependent (s(V),S(V))) / AP-relaxation lower bound + PL heuristics (het).

ACTION COMPOSITION (F1 record, SUPERSEDED AT F7 - the one-shot composed modes mis-stated the information structure, committing the allocation before the demand it allocates against was observed; see DECISION REDEFINITION below and the seq_mask mode, and note the box-rounding KNOWN GAP died with the box mode): two scalar canonical decisions (order, protect) driven by ONE action. Declared with the multi-decision `encodes` list (v0.9.x) as two modes, `discrete` (MultiDiscrete([101,21])) and `box`, which is what the gym has always built; before that the IR carried four half-modes (order_d/protect_d/order_c/protect_c) naming one decision each, with the pairing left to prose - a shape v0.9.5 rejects outright, since the mdp layer consumes both decisions every period and a mode driving one cannot step the env. Homogeneous instances expose only the order dimension (sigma_enabled=false). KNOWN GAP: the `box` mode's component-wise rounding onto the integer decisions is NOT declarable - v0.9.5 forbids a transform on a multi-decision mode and `reparametrize` requires one, so the mode is declared `clip` and the rounding lives in code and in the mode's desc. Demand streams 1-3 are per-segment independent Poissons; Poisson(0) is degenerate-zero for one-hot instances.

RENDERING WIDTHS NAME CONSTANTS (v0.9.0 model layer): pipe.length and adv.length were literals (5, 2) until the model layer was declared; a literal at a width site, for a quantity the theory declares, is how a sweep maximum becomes a capacity limit nobody chose (spec 5.0, model.boundary gate 2). F2 named them pipe_len and T_dl at state_variables.length; F5 found that field is metadata and the width was still a literal one level down, in initial_state's zeros(5) / zeros(2); F6 then replaced the pipe cap outright with the paper's own dimension. See the two entries below.

STATE QUANTITIES WERE MISSING FROM THE MODEL (F5): the paper's state is (x_i, W_i, V_i) and only x_i was declared - `pipe` and `adv` were rendered with widths but named no theory quantity, which is precisely what model.boundary was reporting as 'unpaired caps ... named for no declared quantity, so coverage is unchecked'. Both are now declared with the paper's index ranges (sec 2). The same round found initial_state still carrying zeros(5) / zeros(2): state_variables.length is declarative metadata, and the width that actually sizes the vector is the initial_state expression - so F2's sweep had named the constant at the site that documents the width and missed the site that sets it. Both now name constants. Model fingerprint 3431a2a05046 -> 1d3c1eb91b62, mdp a0a797937d0e -> a89da11f27d3; trajectory byte-identical, differential MATCH x24.

PIPELINE WIDTH IS THE LEAD TIME, NOT A CAP (F6): pipe.length was the constant pipe_len = max(L) + 1 = 5, carried by every instance. The paper is explicit - 'the vector W_i = (w_i, w_{i+1}, ..., w_{i+L-1}) is the supply pipeline' - so the dimension IS L, and eq. (1) is what makes L sufficient: the pipeline shifts FIRST and the new order is inserted last, where the pre-F6 rendering inserted at slot L before shifting and so needed one slot more. Empirically that extra slot was always zero (checked at L=2 and L=4) and at L=0 the whole vector was dead: five permanently-zero observation features on every instance this campaign has ever run. Now length = 'L', initial_state = zeros(L), and the pipe_len constant is deleted. The model fingerprint did NOT move (1d3c1eb91b62): the theory never said 5, only the rendering did. mdp a89da11f27d3 -> 350f6f0445ed. No number moves anywhere - differential MATCH x24, the AP bound still solves to 336.1867, and the plsigma benchmark reproduces -340.452881 to the last digit - but the observation loses its dead slots, so the vec width at L=0 goes 9 -> 4 and BOTH SHIPPED MODELS NO LONGER LOAD (SB3: 'spaces must have the same shape: (9,) != (4,)'). They need retraining, which the F3 re-seed had already made necessary for their numbers.

PIPELINE PADDING IS A GYM CONCERN (F6): a Gym Box is fixed at construction while the state pipeline is now per-instance, so a sampler whose members differ in L (homog_grid spans L 0..4) pads the observation to the family maximum - adi_flex_gym.pipe_obs_slots. A specialist pads nothing and observes exactly its own L slots. The cap did not disappear so much as move to the layer where it is honestly a rendering device, out of the state where it was masquerading as model structure.

DECISION REDEFINITION (F7, 2026-08-17): the second decision is the ALLOCATION (sec 4: 'in addition to the ordering decision, the inventory manager now faces an allocation decision'), not the protection level. sigma parameterizes the sec 4.2 PL *heuristics* - Table 1 classifies its four benchmark models by their allocation POLICY - and declaring it as the decision baked the heuristic family into the action space: every expressible policy was a PL policy, RQ2's discover stance was unreachable by construction, and protect_max=20 silently forbade withholding stock whenever surplus exceeded 20. The model-layer dynamics rule stating the protection cascade as theory is likewise replaced by the free choice it is. Consequences: (i) the two decisions sit at DIFFERENT INFORMATION SETS - order is placed before the period's demand is observed, the allocation at fulfillment after it (sec 2 event sequence) - so the domain becomes two-step (advance1/advance2, spec sec 1.1) and the gym two-phase under one MaskablePPO policy; (ii) at T_dl >= 3 the components are taken sequentially against the residual, so per-step masks can express the coupled constraint sum(a) <= surplus (a gym-level action encoding, the slot pattern - NOT extra MDP periods: nothing stochastic happens between components, and the physical period keeps the demand draw, the costs and the discount tick); (iii) at T_dl = 2 everything degenerates to one masked allocation step; (iv) PL(0)/PL(sigma)/PL(Sigma) become what the paper says they are - feasible POLICIES over the allocation - and sigma survives as their parameterization and as a candidate action ENCODING a = clip(surplus - sigma_action, 0, outstanding), complete only if the sigma range covers the surplus, which is exactly what protect_max=20 failed; (v) alloc_enabled=false (was sigma_enabled) reads 'allocation not live, maximal fill forced' - the same policy sigma=0 encoded, so the homogeneous branch and its exact DP are untouched, and the AP bound is untouched because the relaxation drops the allocation entirely. Two upstream candidates: Decision.feasibility cannot express a state-dependent bound (min(surplus, outstanding)), and nothing declares that decisions within one period sit at different information sets. All solution artifacts predating F7 were already deleted (F3 re-seed + F6 obs change); only the analytic DP/AP tables survive, and they are unaffected The obs feature `phase` (0 = order step, 1 = allocation step) is declared with the placeholder expr '0': the IR has no sub-period concept, so which-decision-am-I-taking is inexpressible - the observational face of candidate (ii). At an allocation step the gym shows info.d as THIS period's realized vector and info.surplus/outstanding as the live feasible-set coordinates; at an order step d is LAST period's vector (the reduced-state vhat information, which the retired vec_d mode existed to carry) and the coordinates are 0.

VECTOR DEMAND DRAW (F8, 2026-08-17): the D event drew the demand vector as T_dl + 1 enumerated (tau = k; dk ~ demand.sample) pairs keyed on tau, a dynamics local, because no family expressed independent-but-not-identically-distributed components. Proposed from this campaign as auto-mdp-solver#49, accepted, shipped v0.9.9 - and NOT adoptable there: a stage-level wrapper could not validate, because the schema's settings loop checked the structural key `of` as an expression (`iid` had the same break since it existed, unnoticed because mab's only iid is a setting-level draw spec that desugars elsewhere). Filed as #52, fixed via a single `families.structural_settings` table both sides split on, released v0.9.10.
